THE CORE IDEA

runs.text: A price floor sets a legal minimum price and is binding only when it lies above the market equilibrium price. A binding floor keeps price from falling to equilibrium, so quantity supplied exceeds quantity demanded and a surplus develops. A floor at or below equilibrium is nonbinding because the market can still reach its equilibrium price.

transcript.sourceText: The market equilibrium is $30 and 200 units. A binding floor of $40 holds price above equilibrium; sellers offer 250 units while buyers demand 150. The resulting surplus is 250 - 150 = 100 units, so some output remains unsold at the controlled price.
